title: Share useful data. Respect each business’s boundaries.
summary: How can a bank serve the same person across legal entities without sharing every relationship, every field or every location? This synthetic lab makes those choices visible.

title: Why this lab exists.
summary: Explore useful sharing across bank businesses without treating identity, access and location as the same decision.

title: See both the legal and physical footprint.
summary: The control plane answers who may use the data and where each authorised copy resides.

title: Test the contradiction, not just the happy path.
summary: Entity permission is necessary; it is never enough on its own.

title: Desired state is not observed state.
summary: Separate policy permission, physical copy presence and destination acknowledgement.

title: Entity sovereignty, physical placement.
summary: Separate the business federation boundary from the database deployment boundary.

title: Operate stores; govern entities.
summary: Infrastructure management and customer federation remain distinct control planes.

title: Authenticate the entity. Resolve the store.
summary: Business API access needs both legal-entity context and a permitted physical processing location.

title: Permission meets physical reality.
summary: OPA evaluates the recipient legal entity and the actual resolved storage country together.

title: One owner transaction. Explicit federation.
summary: Keep local business invariants atomic and make remote projection progress observable.

title: Placement and entitlement are separate problems.
summary: Choose a transport after the ownership, exclusion and physical-boundary rules are explicit.

title: Move the approved projection, not the customer universe.
summary: Candidate legal entities are resolved and checked before any destination receives identifying data.

title: Revoke access. Reconcile copies. Prove each step.
summary: Policy changes and entity relocation are different workflows with different completion evidence.

title: Make the remaining decisions visible.
summary: The prototype chooses small, reversible implementation boundaries while retaining the harder questions.

title: Observe the fleet without exporting its customers.
summary: Entity and store dimensions explain movement; customer data stays out of telemetry.

title: Evidence for each legal and physical boundary.
summary: Receipts must identify both the recipient entity and the actual storage destination.

title: Entity-aware contracts from the first request.
summary: API routes identify a relationship record; its owner and global identity remain explicit data.

title: An executable thin slice, with explicit next gates.
summary: Continue from the validated container lab; earn each pilot capability with its own acceptance evidence.

title: Sources, assumptions and verification.
summary: The executable policy checks and design assumptions are documented separately from deployment claims.

title: One person. Separate banking relationships.
summary: Knowing who someone is does not tell every bank entity what it may see or change.

title: An entity directory is not a relocation switch.
summary: Bind entities to approved physical stores, then evaluate every candidate crossing against that binding.

title: Global party. Federated relationships.
summary: Two independent distribution paths on top of one coherent party relationship model.

title: A parallel control layer. Explicit joins.
summary: Table defaults establish the contract. Business keys and context determine which rows may cross.

title: Keep business services. Add governed federation.
summary: Reuse existing banking services. A loosely coupled sovereignty layer governs location and movement; business services retain the interactions.

title: Engineer for the work. Budget for the tails.
summary: 50 million parties, 100 million relationships, explicit p95/p99 targets and reproducible capacity scenarios.

title: Prove correctness. Then earn the scale.
summary: A gated backlog with named ownership, dependencies and measurable exit evidence.

title: Operational work keeps its own capacity.
summary: Decouple the cost of changing placement from the small act of changing authority. Policy campaigns cannot sit ahead of operational records.

title: Bring the legal entity home.
summary: Add Mumbai as a fourth physical store, move the India entity while source operations continue, then change authority once and account for old copies.
